# Backlog

Living document — items deferred from earlier sessions plus future ideas with
the reasoning for the deferral. Update when items ship or new ideas land.

## Active themes

### Data foundation (current focus)
Building out player, team, and environmental data coverage so future modeling
work has rich features to draw from. Examples in progress or queued below.

### Daily ops + iteration
Predict → evaluate → improve → export, with incremental fixes as exports surface
issues. Park factors and reliever-as-starter fix shipped recently in this mode.

---

## Feature backlog

Roughly ordered by expected value vs effort. Items marked **[DEFERRED]** have a
specific reason they're not being built now.

**2026-10-15 — DONE (ARCHITECT 2026-10-15 10:16 ET, addendum 74 item 2): the pitcher probe prints the games with neither starter, their months and provenance, and whether a sync-appearances re-run fills them (#507, #535).**
- **Item 2, verbatim:** "THE PITCHER RECEIPT'S MISSING LINE (addendum 72 item 2; #507; small, read-only): scripts/mlb_pitcher_probe.py prints, for each season, the games with neither starter recorded: their date range, count by month, and which sync wrote them (whatever provenance column the row carries; print which you used). Then, from the code, whether a re-run of the sync that writes pitcher_appearances over that range would fill them or a command is missing — one sentence in the probe's output, from a read of the sync, not a guess. The run is mine (Friday's block)."
- **Read for it (law 1):**
  - The only writer of pitcher_appearances is `cli.py sync-appearances` (MLB, `--season`, default `--backfill`, `--limit 2000`, `--refresh`).
  - It targets a finished game by its statsapi id (`matches.external_ids['mlb_stats_api']`, the baseball adapter's source) when no row's `source_game_id` holds that id.
  - It skips a game whose id has rows unless `--refresh`, and skips a game with no statsapi id always. It takes at most `--limit` targets (default 2000), in no set order.
  - `--refresh` makes every finished game with a statsapi id a target, and deletes their rows, committed before any request. A request that fails or returns nothing leaves that game with no rows.
  - `MLBStatsAPIAdapter.get_game_pitcher_appearances` marks a starter only where the boxscore's per-game `stats.pitching.gamesStarted` is 1. Its docstring names a max-outs fallback that the code does not have. So rows written are not a starter restored (Codex on #535).
  - The provenance a matches row carries is its `external_ids` keys; pitcher_appearances itself carries only `captured_at`.
- The probe's sentence states that reading with the season's own counts.

In a 12:30pm-3:00pm ET block those fixtures get their T-15 poll only, printed as missed before it and counted apart. The 21:00 CEST kickoffs (3:00pm ET) get all seven polls (T-120 at 1:00pm ET). **2026-10-15 — DONE (ARCHITECT 2026-10-15 10:16 ET, addendum 74 item 3): the #425 receipt isolates the one-sided-list guard, per case, on and off; the cases only the guard changed are counted (#536).**
- **Item 3, verbatim:** "THE #425 RECEIPT ISOLATES THE ONE-SIDED-LIST GUARD (before Monday's 120-case ruling): the review of 10-14 noted that the receipt code does not isolate the guard, so the 120 cases cannot say what the guard alone changed. Code reads the receipt's code, says in the PR body what it measures today, and adds the isolation: for each case, the Desk's call with the guard on and with it off (the rule's own switch, the way the other rule_off contexts work), and the receipt counts the cases where only the guard changed the call. Measurement only; no rule, threshold or switch default changes. Tests on the receipt's own fixtures."
- **What it measured before #536:** the injury FACTOR. That is log-loss of the stored probabilities (the cut kept) against the same game re-priced with the cut taken out, overall, by list-length difference, and on the +5pp cohort. The receipt never read the Desk, so the guard (desk_policy's one-sided-list rule, addendum 40 item 6) was in none of its figures. "0.9921 with the one-sided rule against 1.0003 without" (addendum 63 item 1) is the cut kept against taken out, not the guard on against off.
- **In #536:** the Desk's call per case, with the guard as it stands and with its own switch off. Every other switch is as it stands, so a call that differs is a call only the guard changed. The receipt also counts the one-sided cases an earlier rule reached first (by kind), and grades each changed call by its own instrument.
- **The Desk input, stated in the receipt:** as of the prediction's computed_at, with the book reference the predictions export read then. That reference is not the grading close, which is read at kickoff.
  - Since #167 `sync_odds` replaces the odds rows on every sync and appends the same consensus to `odds_snapshots`. So the session read at computed_at is the latest one by then in either table.
  - Where neither table has one by then but the odds table holds a later one, the session read then may have been replaced (an unpriced sync writes no snapshot, and before #167 no sync did). The case is counted as reference unknown and not evaluated.
  - The database holds no published desk block, so a call here can still differ from the one published on the day: an export rebuilt after computed_at can carry a later book session.
- **No Kalshi quote is given.** Kalshi snapshots exist. On a three-way soccer row the Desk takes no Kalshi-only reference, so a quote changes a call's units (the executable-cost gate), never the call. Both runs read the same input, which is what isolates the guard.

**2026-10-14 — RULED (ARCHITECT 2026-10-14 10:01 ET, addendum 67 item 1): the Kalshi settled-market history ingest, `kalshi-history`, writing one new table, `kalshi_settled_markets` (#519).**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "KALSHI SETTLED-MARKET HISTORY, the ingest (K-track data lane; the Issue of addendum 66 item 6 is its ticket). What it is: a stored record of every settled Kalshi game market in our series, with the last two-sided quote before kickoff, so the backtests and the older-season tests have a Kalshi close where no book close exists. Read-only against the exchange (public endpoints, no key); it writes ONE new table and nothing else — no odds snapshot, no close used by grading, no prediction row is touched; grading keeps reading what it reads today until a later ruling says otherwise. - Command: `python cli.py kalshi-history --series KXMLBGAME [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--dry-run] [--max-calls N]`. One series per run. --dry-run lists what would be stored and stores nothing. Default --max-calls 300 (the probe's whole run was 241 calls); the run stops cleanly at the cap and prints where it stopped (the cursor), so the next run resumes; never a retry loop on a non-200. - Sources, both: `/historical/markets?series_ticker=…` (settled before the cutoff; page by cursor) and `/markets?series_ticker=…&status=settled` (settled after it). Candles: `/historical/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks` for the first, `/series/{s}/markets/{t}/candlesticks` for the second, period_interval=1, start_ts = kickoff − 6h, end_ts = close_time. The two candle shapes differ (historical: yes_bid.close / yes_ask.close / volume / open_interest; live: close_dollars / volume_fp / open_interest_fp); read each by its own keys from the kept payloads of 2026-10-14 under logs/ (law 1: enumerate the keys from those files, not from memory); a null price in a zero-volume minute is left null, never filled. - Table `kalshi_settled_markets`: ticker (unique), event_ticker, series, side ('HOME' | 'AWAY' | 'DRAW' | null), match_id (nullable), yes_sub_title, kalshi_result ('yes' | 'no' | null), close_time, settled_time, source ('historical' | 'live'), fetched_at, last_ts (the end_period_ts of the last candle at or before kickoff that carries both a bid and an ask), last_bid, last_ask, last_mid, candles_6h (count), candles_two_sided (count), gaps (minutes missing in the 6h window), raw_first_candle (json), notes. - Matching: the market's event day and the two names go through the shared matcher as the live sync does (src/ingestion/kalshi_match, the same fit, the same pins, the same refusals) against the stored games of that day; a refusal stores the row with match_id null and the refusal reason in notes — refused rows are kept, never guessed, and are listed at the end of the run by reason, like the replay does. - Kickoff for the window: the stored game's kickoff when matched; when unmatched, the ticker's date-and-time when the ticker carries a clock (the MLB shape), else no candles are fetched and notes says so. - Receipts at the end of every run: markets listed / stored / already stored / refused by reason; candle calls made; rows with last_ts null (no two-sided candle before kickoff); the cutoff read at the start. - Tests on the kept payloads (both shapes, the cutoff file, a settled page and a historical page), with a throwaway DB: a stored row's last_bid/last_ask come from the right keys for each shape; a null-price minute stays null; an unmatched market stores match_id null with its reason; the cap stops the run and prints the cursor; --dry-run writes nothing. Gate-class contract fields are not touched, so no backtest is owed; this is an ingest. PR body: the receipt of a --dry-run on KXMLBGAME --since 2026-10-01 is enough (a real pull is the operator's block, after my read)."
- **As built:** src/ingestion/kalshi_history.py, the command, migrate_kalshi_settled_markets.py and tests/test_kalshi_history.py. The table is written and nothing else; nothing reads it as a close until a later ruling.
- **How the matcher is read for a settled market:**
  - These refusals are the matcher's own, unchanged: no pair, no date, no fit, a pair tie, two rows, a date tie, the time gate, no game on the date, a time tie, a side tie, an unknown yes team, two claims (read across events, as one place() call reads it).
  - Four refusals of the live sync are conditions of an open market and cannot hold for a settled one, so they are not read:
    - in play (`now` is set before every game);
    - no price;
    - the spread guard (a settled market's quote is its candles');
    - the run's window (the window here is --since/--until).
  - Each event is placed alone, so "behind an event out of step", a rule between open events, never fires.
- **Law 1, read (addendum 68 items 3 and 5):** the payloads' keys (`kalshi_history.KEYS`) are enumerated from the five kept files of 2026-10-14 11:54Z.
  - Source: the operator's branch laptop/kalshi-payloads-1014 (34723f1), tests/fixtures/kalshi_history/raw/. The raw files never land on main; the branch is deleted after #521 merges.
  - Which key differed: no key of the receipt (addendum 66 item 6) or of the probe's reader differs from the files.
    - The cutoff is `market_settled_ts`, and the lists are `markets` / `cursor`.
    - The market keys are `ticker` / `event_ticker` / `yes_sub_title` / `result` / `close_time`.
    - Historical candles read `yes_bid.close` / `yes_ask.close`, live candles read `yes_bid.close_dollars` / `yes_ask.close_dollars`, and both carry `end_period_ts`.
  - settled_time's key, which the receipt did not name, is `settlement_ts`. It is on all 200 markets of each kept page; the column was null until now.
  - Read in the files besides the keys:
    - A price is a dollar string, and end_period_ts is epoch seconds.
    - A time is ISO with a fraction of 0 to 6 digits.
    - A zero-volume minute of the historical shape carries `price.close` / `open` / `high` / `low` / `mean` null, with `price.previous` set and its bid and ask present (42 of the 292 historical candles; the live reply has none).
    - An empty side of a market's book is sent at size zero (`yes_bid_size_fp` / `yes_ask_size_fp` "0.00" on all 400 markets), priced 0.00 for a bid and 1.00 for an ask (0.00 on the two legs of KXNFLGAME-26JAN25LASEA).
    - A tied NFL game settles both legs as result "scalar" (0.50): 2 of 200 historical, 4 of 200 live. That is stored as kalshi_result null with "result as read: 'scalar'" in notes; the table holds 'yes', 'no' or null.
  - The fixtures are the kept files trimmed: whole objects only, in the kept order and the kept format (tests/fixtures/kalshi_history/README.md names the raw files' sha256 and the rule).
    - The cutoff file is byte for byte.
    - Each page keeps three events (six markets) of its 100 events (200 markets).
    - Each candle reply keeps every candle up to the kickoff the tests store, and the five after it.
- **From the review of the kept-payload commit (an adversarial review, each finding verified by reproduction):**
  - **Two-sided is ruling 9's predicate:** `0 < bid <= ask < 1` (#286, ARCHITECT 2026-10-06, "two-sided = 0 < bid <= ask < 1"; `k_receipt.leg_two_sided`).
    - The files send an empty side at size zero, priced 0.00 (a bid) or 1.00 (an ask). Read as a price, a minute with no bid became the stored quote with a mid of ask/2.
    - In the kept replies such minutes come only after the games end, so no stored value of the kept data changes.
    - This reading of ruling 9 here is for the architect's read on #521.
  - **A fraction of 4 or 5 digits is read whole on Python 3.10** (docs/CLI.md says 3.10+). There, fromisoformat takes only 3 or 6 digits.
    - Without the fix, settled_time was null on 58 of the 400 kept markets.
    - A close_time of 4 or 5 digits (16 of 200 historical) read as missing, and the market was stored with no quote and never asked again.
  - **The --dry-run receipt prints each row's settled_time,** and the run prints how many rows have none.
  - **Tests strengthened where the rewrite on the kept files had weakened them:**
    - the close leaf of each shape on kept minutes whose open / high / low differ;
    - a cap and a failed page or returning cursor in the second list, after the first is read whole;
    - --until's own day;
    - a stored first candle whose price is null;
    - a kept historical page row's result and settled_time;
    - an unreadable timestamp inside the window.
- **Codex P2 on #521 (e988275), fixed: the write gate reads the migration's own marker, not the table.**
  - `KalshiSettledMarket` is mapped, so any `init_db()` (create_all, run by many scheduled commands) creates the table. A run could then write before the backed-up migration ran.
  - migrate_kalshi_settled_markets.py now writes a one-row marker, `kalshi_settled_markets_migration`, by Core SQL. It is unmapped, so create_all never makes it. This is the convention of `ncaa_cfbd.MIGRATION_MARKER` (Codex on #333) and `V2_MIGRATION_MARKER` (#367).
  - A run without --dry-run refuses unless the table AND the marker's row exist. --dry-run still reads without either.
  - **Codex's second P2 (on f0a564f), fixed as the rest of the same fix:** `drop_db()` (`init-db --force`) now drops the marker too.
    - drop_all() drops only mapped tables. A forced reset therefore left the marker beside a recreated empty table, and the gate read "migrated".
    - `drop_db()` already drops the two CFBD markers for this reason (#333), so the convention cited above has two legs. The first push carried only one.

- **#490, ruled in (addendum 60 item 3, verbatim, with one sentence replaced by addendum 61 item 4):** "A pull request that changes docs/roadmap.json is checked against the file on its base. For each lane both sides hold, by its lane id: an earliest_live that differs, and a due that differs on a step both sides hold, needs a moved line on the head. A step is the same step where its what is the same, word for word. The moved line's which is the word earliest_live, or the step's what, word for word; its was is the base's date and its now is the head's. A date set where the base had none needs no moved line. An earliest_live cleared needs its moved line, with now null. A lane or a step that only one side holds needs nothing from this check: the ruling the pull request quotes carries it, and I read it. The check fails the pull request and names the lane and the date. It never rewrites the file."
  - Also: "within a lane no two steps share a what."
  - Where: beside check-fragments, in the job that already reads the base.
- **#492, ruled (addendum 61 item 4, verbatim):** "Setting a first earliest_live is not a move and needs no moved line. Clearing one is a move, and it is how a failed run is written: its moved line has which earliest_live, was the date, now null, and why. In a moved line now may be null where which is earliest_live; was is always a real date. A step's due is never cleared: a step is done, moved, or removed by a quoted ruling."

  - It exits 0 when the file is unchanged or every move has its line, and 1 naming each lane and date otherwise (or a head that is not UTF-8, not JSON, or does not validate). It exits 2 when the base cannot be read. It never writes the file.

**2026-10-12 — FINDING + RULED + BUILT (ARCHITECT 2026-10-12 17:38 ET, addendum 54 items 5 and 6; 18:20 ET, addendum 55 items 3 and 4; #476, lane #478): a postponement inside a series puts the next game's Kalshi market on the postponed game's row; on a clock series, an event out of step holds the later events of its two names. PR #477.**
- **Finding (#476), attributed to the architect's read and harness:** Kalshi's rule (`rules_secondary` of KXMLBGAME-26OCT132000CLETB-TB, read through the public API by web fetch at about 5:30pm ET): "If this game is postponed or delayed, the market will remain open and close after the rescheduled game has finished (within two days). If the game is cancelled or rescheduled to over two days away, the market will resolve to a fair price in accordance with the rules." So a postponed game keeps its event, dated the day first scheduled, and the next game of the series keeps its own. On the ALCS shapes (Game 3, 26OCT151800TBCLE, rained out and played Friday 6pm ET; Game 4, 26OCT161800TBCLE, moved to Saturday; the run Friday 11am ET), main and the switch both store the two legs of 26OCT161800TBCLE on Game 3's row. The leg guard stops it only where the later row still holds current legs of the same event. The row shows the next game's prices, and its order line carries the next game's ticker. Not established: whether it has happened on stored legs.
- **Ruling (verbatim, beside addendum 52 item 4, which stands):** "On a series whose ticker carries a clock time, the events of the same two names are read together. An event with no game number is out of step when no game of its two teams is on its date, or when its date is before the day of the run. Dates are read in US Eastern, and a row that is not a game is not one here. No event of the same two names dated after an event out of step is placed in that run, with or without a game number: it is refused under a reason of its own, and its line names the earliest event out of step and says why that one is. Events dated before the earliest one are placed as ruled."
- **As built (src/ingestion/kalshi_match.py):** `behind_out_of_step` reads every event of a clock series before any is placed. It groups events by their two names (case-folded) and reads every market, priced or not. "No game of its two teams on its date" is read on the pair place() would choose (the best fit on the event's day); no fit at all is no game. A market of a later-dated event of the same names that would otherwise take its place on a game is refused under "behind an event of the same two names out of step" (addendum 55 item 3, below). Its line reads `✗ <event>: refused behind <earliest>, out of step: <why>`. The event out of step keeps its own reason (no fit, no game on its date, in play, outside the window). A date-only series is outside the rule.
- **Ruled (addendum 55 item 3, 18:20 ET), verbatim:** "The reason 'behind' and its line are for a market that would otherwise have been placed. A market refused for a reason of its own keeps that reason, and no such line is printed for it." Why: on today's seven open events, on the rows as stored at 4:27pm, the first build refused three later events as behind, with a line each (26OCT161800TBCLE, 26OCT151800TBCLE, 26OCT152000MILLAD). None of them could have been placed, because tomorrow's rows are not stored. Every run of a normal day would print such lines, dozens in a regular season, and the one line that matters would be lost. The architect's sentence of addendum 54 ("it is refused under a reason of its own") let it be built so. As built now: the check sits where a market would take its place on a game, after the window, the side and the in-play test, before the two-claims count. The three shapes of the finding refuse as behind as before, with their lines. No placement moves: the markets it now leaves to their own reasons were refused before as well.
- **LANE (#478, addendum 55 item 4, attributed; nothing built now):** our MLB rows are held one day ahead. So addendum 52's no-game line prints for each pair's next-day event on every run: one or two a day now, fifteen in a regular season. Before Opening Day 2027, either hold the schedule as far as Kalshi lists it, or quiet that line.
- **What it costs (ruled):** the rule only refuses. While Kalshi has not settled yesterday's market of a pair, today's is refused, and the line says so. On the evening of a rainout, the next game's event is refused though its row is right (the receipt's third shape).

**2026-10-12 — RULED + BUILT, FIRST OF TWO PRS (ARCHITECT 2026-10-10, addendum 37 item 2; day rule 2026-10-12, addendum 44 item 1; how the receipt is taken, addendum 50 item 6; finding #413): the Kalshi matcher's module, its tests and a read-only replay. PR #461. The switch of the two sync paths is a PR of its own, called on the replay's console.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "A Kalshi market is stored on a game only when its event fits that game: the event's two team names, taken from the event's own markets, fit the game's two teams, one each. One name alone never places a market. Names decide before time: the fit is judged among the stored games of the series' own competition on the event's day, and when the best fit is shared by games of two different pairs of teams the market is refused. The time gate and the run's window then choose only among games of that one pair, and exactly one must pass. A worse-fitting game never takes a market because the best one was outside the window or the gate. Two markets that claim the same side of the same game in one run are both refused. Every refusal is counted by its reason."
- **Day rule (verbatim):** "The event's day is the date in its ticker, read as a US Eastern day. A game is on the event's day when its stored kickoff, read in US Eastern, falls on that date or a day either side. On a series whose ticker carries no clock time that is the whole time gate: occurrence_datetime is an expected expiration, and there it places nothing and refuses nothing. Inside the one pair, a game on the ticker's own date takes the market before a game a day off; where the date cannot separate two games of the pair, the event's markets are refused. Where the ticker carries a clock time, the time gate stays as built, inside the one pair."
- **The receipt (addendum 50 6(b), verbatim):** "The switch is a PR of its own. First, and by itself, main takes the new module, its tests and a read-only replay; the two sync paths stay as they are. The replay fetches each series' open markets once, places them with the new module on the stored games, opened read-only, and stores nothing. For each series it prints what the new module places and what it refuses, by reason, beside the legs main's matcher stored at its last sync, and then every leg that differs: on another game or side, stored by main and refused now, placed now and not stored by main. The operator runs it in the morning block, straight after the day's Kalshi syncs. The switch PR carries that console, and I call it on that."
- **Rows that are not games (addendum 50 6(c), verbatim):** "A row whose status is cancelled, postponed or stale orphan is not a game for the matcher: it takes no market and is not counted among the rows of a pair."
- **The architect's read of the mirror (addendum 50 6(a)):** 930 stored legs of ten series; KXMLBGAME alone carries a clock (38 of 38); 926 legs sit on a game on the ticker's own ET date; the other four are on Florida A&M's game played a day early (two its own, two the Alabama legs main put there). For the time, the day rule drops no leg main placed rightly. Accepted as built (6(d)): a best fit shared by two pairs is refused even where one fits whole and the other by one word of a longer name; the replay's count is read before more is asked.
- **Next:** the operator runs `python cli.py kalshi-replay` in the morning block straight after the Kalshi syncs and sends the console and the kept markets file; the switch PR carries that console. #413 stays open.

- **The doubleheader gate (#461's P1, built in 2d5593b; verbatim):** "On a series whose ticker carries a clock time, an event whose ticker carries a game number (G1, G2) is admitted by that clock alone: a game of the pair passes only when its stored kickoff is within two hours of it. occurrence_datetime admits no game to such an event. A time-tie refusal prints its line (Kalshi's clock and occurrence, each passing game's id and kickoff); it rides the switch PR with #470 items 2 and 3.

**2026-10-09 — BUILT (ARCHITECT addendum 31 item 1; Issue #387): `sync_odds` orders its candidates by kickoff, then id, before the limit; `--limit` now means the next N.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "sync_odds orders its candidates by kickoff, then id, before the limit is applied, so that the limit means the next N. --match-ids is unchanged."
- **Amendment (ARCHITECT 2026-10-09 19:07 ET, addendum 33 item 2, verbatim):** "The review's finding is real. Your fix keeps my sentence to the letter, and the letter pins a defect: a named list longer than the limit is cut, silently, and the CLI's default limit is 20. The entry's "(no limit)" for the closing runs was not so."
  - "AMENDED: A named game is never dropped by the limit. With --match-ids every named game is priced and --limit does not apply. The order is kickoff, then id, in both modes."
- The change: `IngestionService.sync_odds` (src/ingestion/service.py) orders its candidate query by `Match.utc_date, Match.id` in both modes; `--limit` cuts the list only when no `--match-ids` is given. **Until this PR the limit cut a named list:** `--match-ids` with more games than `--limit` (CLI default 20) priced only the first N in storage order, silently. The `--limit` and `--match-ids` help say so. (The first fix, 8fb84ee, kept the named list as on main, cut included; replaced by this amendment.)
- What it changes: the window service plans `sync-odds --competition C --season S --limit max(n6, 1)` (deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:129-130), n6 being that competition's non-finished games starting before the far-tier edge; that limit now prices the competition's next n6 SCHEDULED games by kickoff, not the first n6 in storage order. The comment in deploy/hosting/chains.py:234-235 ("sync_odds takes the next N scheduled games") is now true. The closing runs price by `--match-ids`: until this PR a closing run naming more than 20 games through `sync-odds` would have had its list cut by the default limit; now every named game is priced.
- Receipt: tests/test_sync_odds_next_n.py, both tests fail on main and pass here: the limit test (`['late', 'mid'] == ['early', 'mid']`) and `test_a_named_game_is_never_dropped_by_the_limit` (`['late', 'mid'] == ['early', 'mid', 'late']`).

**2026-10-09 — FINDING (ARCHITECT addendum 23 item 3 F(1), logged, nothing built; Issue #387; #385): `sync_odds` (soccer) applies `--limit` with no ORDER BY, and the window service relies on it.** The ruling: "F. FINDINGS TO LOG, a BACKLOG entry and an Issue each, nothing built: (1) sync_odds (soccer) applies --limit with no ORDER BY, and the window service relies on it".
- The code: `IngestionService.sync_odds` (src/ingestion/service.py:708-726) builds `select(Match).where(Match.competition_id == comp.id)` plus the season and the SCHEDULED / `utc_date >= now` filters, with no `.order_by(...)`; it collects the rows in the order SQLite returns them and then cuts `candidates = candidates[:limit]` (service.py:725-726). Which N games are priced is therefore the table's storage order, not "the next N".
- Who relies on it: the window service plans `sync-odds --competition C --season S --limit <that competition's window game count>` (deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:129-130, `max(int(n6 or 0), 1)`), on the premise written in deploy/hosting/chains.py:234-235: "sync_odds takes the next N scheduled games". When storage order is not kick-off order (a re-keyed or late-created row, a game moved by a re-sync), the window can price a later game and leave an earlier one in the window unpriced.

**2026-10-09 — RULING + FIX (ARCHITECT addendum 30 items 3 and 4): the NCAA placeholder re-key, amending the second re-key ruling of 2026-10-05; the laptop morning chain reads NCAA by date before it refreshes by id.**
- **Ruling, item 3 (verbatim):** "For NCAA, a stored SCHEDULED row at the provider's TBD kickoff holds its natural key for its whole game day. An unknown incoming id for the same home and away team, at a real kickoff within 24 hours of that placeholder, re-keys that row. Every refusal of the 12-hour rule applies as it stands: the stored id still in the listing, a row already claimed in the run, more than one candidate, the pair swapped. A row at a real kickoff keeps the 12-hour window."
  - "What a placeholder is, and what resolves one, is already ruled (2026-10-05) and already in code: is_placeholder_kickoff and placeholder_resolved in scripts/ncaa_rekey_receipt.py. One definition, shared; not a second copy."
  - "NFL is untouched: we hold no receipt for how the provider marks an unannounced NFL time."
  - "The rows already doubled are not this PR's. The operator merges them with dedupe-matches --orphans, dry run first, on my word."
- **Ruling, item 4 (verbatim):** "The laptop's morning chain reads NCAA by date for today to today+7, one day per call, and then runs refresh-by-id, as ncaa-schedule does on the host. After a re-key the listing reads carry the new ids and the refresh confirms them; in the other order every re-keyed game prints as not found."
- **Amendment (ARCHITECT 2026-10-09 19:07 ET, addendum 33 item 1, verbatim):** "One amendment before I call it. "More than one candidate", as I wrote it, lets a placeholder row take a match away from the 12-hour rule. Take a doubled game: the placeholder row and its second row at the real kickoff. If the provider re-issues that game's id again, main re-keys the second row. Under eb53a44 the two rows are two candidates, and the listing is refused at every read until someone merges the pair; the live row stops updating. The host's file of 16:00Z today held 27 such pairs."
  - "AMENDED: The placeholder window is consulted only where the 12-hour rule would create a row: no candidate within 12 hours, same pair or swapped. It never takes a match away from the 12-hour rule. There the same refusals apply among placeholder rows: the stored id still in the listing, a row already claimed in the run, more than one placeholder candidate, the pair swapped."
  - "So the fix can only turn what main would create into a re-key or a refusal, and everything the 12-hour rule decides today it decides tomorrow."
- **Built:**
  - `src/ingestion/placeholder.py`: `is_placeholder_kickoff` and `placeholder_resolved`, moved verbatim from `scripts/ncaa_rekey_receipt.py`; the script imports them (the receipt's accounting is unchanged).
  - `src/ingestion/service.py`: `PLACEHOLDER_REKEY_COMPETITIONS = {"NCAA"}`; in `IngestionService._rekey_candidate` the 12-hour rule decides first, exactly as on main: any stored row of the pair, same or swapped, within `REKEY_WINDOW_H` (12h) of the incoming kickoff. Only when it has no candidate (where main would create a row) and the competition is NCAA, the placeholder window is consulted: the SCHEDULED rows for which `placeholder_resolved(stored, incoming)` holds (stored at 04:00:00Z, incoming at a non-placeholder kickoff within 24h), with the same refusals among them (stored id still listed, claimed in the run, more than one placeholder candidate, swapped pair). - **Readings:** "within 24 hours of that placeholder" is `placeholder_resolved`'s own `abs(post - pre) <= 24h`, either side of 04:00Z (one definition, not a second); an incoming id itself at a placeholder time is not a "real kickoff" and gets the 12-hour window only. The pair-swapped refusal uses the same widened window (it is one of "every refusal of the 12-hour rule"). Only rows with status SCHEDULED get the widened window.

Further tests: beyond 24h a second row is created; the stored-id-still-listed, claimed and swapped refusals apply under the 24h window; the doubled game (a placeholder row and a real-kickoff row 10.5h from the incoming) re-keys the real-kickoff row, as on main, and leaves the placeholder row untouched (addendum 33 item 1: fails on eb53a44, `(0, 1, 3) != (0, 2, 2)`); two placeholder rows for one pair are refused; NFL with a 04:00Z row keeps the 12-hour window; the script and the sync share the same function objects.

**2026-10-09 — FINDING + FIX (ARCHITECT addendum 19 item 3, track H, host only): the host's college kickoff times were stale. A daily forward-week NCAA sync now keeps them fresh.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "NEW FINDING, host only: the host's college kickoff times are stale. At 11:06Z today the host's window card (0023368) showed 30 of Saturday's games at 2026-10-10T04:00Z, the provider's placeholder, inside its 24-hour window, with no books and no Kalshi on any of them. The laptop's file of 2026-10-08 21:56Z has announced kickoffs for 27 of the 30 (Georgia at Alabama 23:30Z), and its file of 2026-10-06 already had 91 of Saturday's 95. Yesterday's 16:00Z host fixtures file had 38 placeholders against the laptop's 4. It is why I did not count 2026-10-08 as a clean compare day: by the Exhibit 1 precedent a chain gap is not an explained class.
Open an Issue (track H, finding, ncaa). Cause first, from the code and the provider's responses (law 1): the host's ncaa-market chain syncs yesterday and today only, and the hourly window service had these games inside its window for seven hours without moving them. Say what each of the two does for an NCAA game two days out and for one inside the window, and how the provider marks an unannounced time, if it does.
Then the fix, its own small PR, before the next tag: 'On the host, the stored kickoff of every NCAA game in the next seven days is at most one day old.' One test that fails on today's chain."
- **Cause, from the code (the host runs v1.3.0):**
  - Only `sync-matches` writes a stored kickoff. For a provider id already stored, `_apply_match_updates` overwrites `utc_date` unconditionally (`src/ingestion/service.py:429`). The american-football adapter sends `date` only when from == to (`src/adapters/api_american_football.py:208-209`).
  - **ncaa-market at v1.3.0:** single-day syncs of `{yesterday}` and `{today}` (v1.3.0 `deploy/hosting/chains.py:172-174`), timer Thu/Fri 16:00 and Sat 13:00 UTC. Main added `{tomorrow}` and Tue/Wed (#320, not in v1.3.0). A game two days out is never fetched. A game inside the window is fetched only on a run whose yesterday/today/tomorrow includes its UTC date. The Thu 10-08 16:00Z run synced 10-07 and 10-08 only, which is why that day's host fixtures file had 38 placeholders.
  - **The window service (hourly):** a game two days out is outside its query (`m.utc_date >= now AND < now+24h`, `deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:94`), so the window plans no step for it. A game inside the window gets a single-day sync of each UTC date in {now, now+24h} (`sp_run.py:103`, `:118-120`). So from 06:05Z on 10-09 every run called NCAA `date=2026-10-10`.
  - **The window question is not settled by the code.** That call overwrites the kickoff of every stored id the provider lists. So those 30 ids were not listed with an announced time on the window's `date=2026-10-10` responses. Either (a) the date-filtered listing still carried 04:00Z for them, or (b) the announced time came under a new provider id. In case (b) a new id whose kickoff is more than `REKEY_WINDOW_H = 12` hours from the stored 04:00Z (23:30Z is 19.5h away) is not re-keyed onto the placeholder row (`service.py:72`, `:490-491`). It is created as a second row, and the placeholder row is left untouched. The step receipts settle it: the window's NCAA `sync-matches` lines in `receipts.jsonl` between 06:05Z and 11:05Z on 10-09 show `created`/`updated`, and `scripts/kickoff_receipt.py --find "Alabama" --date 2026-10-10` prints the stored row and the provider's raw date block for its id. Neither is run here (no host, no key).
- **How the provider marks an unannounced time:** the only repo evidence is the 2026-10-05 architect ruling, encoded in `scripts/ncaa_rekey_receipt.py:234-236`: "The provider's TBD kickoff: 04:00:00Z (midnight US Eastern)". The adapter reads only `date.timestamp` (`api_american_football.py:233-236`) and `status.short` (`:243-245`, unknown codes become SCHEDULED, no TBD code in `_STATUS`). No code reads `date.time`, and the repo holds no recorded NCAA `/games` payload. So whether the provider also flags the time (for example a `time` of "TBD", or a status code) cannot be determined from repo evidence.
- **Fix:**
  - New host chain `ncaa-schedule`: single-day NCAA `sync-matches` for today..today+7, sync only.
  - New timer `sp-ncaa-schedule.timer`, every day at 10:35 and 22:35 UTC. ncaa-market runs Tue-Sat, and one failed run still leaves the kickoff under a day old.
  - `{today_plus1..7}` date vars.
  - ncaa-market, the window and the adapter are unchanged.
- **Limit (law 4):** if the cause is (b), a sync refreshes the new id's row and leaves a 04:00Z twin. That is the existing `dedupe-matches --orphans` class. The invariant then holds for every live provider id, not for the orphan. The receipts above decide whether this needs its own ruling.
- **Receipt:** `test_every_ncaa_kickoff_in_the_next_seven_days_is_refreshed_every_day` fails on the old chains ("Mon 2026-10-05: NCAA kickoffs never refreshed for ['2026-10-05', … '2026-10-12']") and passes on the new ones.
- **Amended by ARCHITECT addendum 21 item 1 (2026-10-09 08:55 ET): the cause is found, and the refresh is by id.**
  - **Receipts (verbatim, operator console on the laptop, 2026-10-09 12:27Z and 12:47Z):** "The season listing (league 2, season 2026) holds 841 games: FT 765, AOT 23, CANC 1, PST 1, NS 51; 39 have a team name missing. On the UTC days 2026-10-09, 10 and 11 it lists 0, 2 and 1 games. The by-date listing for those days returns the same games as the season listing: ids 24573 and 24583 on 10-10, 24199 on 10-11. The two readings do not differ. Of the laptop's 97 SCHEDULED NCAA rows kicking off in the next 72 hours, 96 carry a provider id that is not in the season listing. By id they answer: /games?id=23653 resolves Georgia at Alabama, 2026-10-10 23:30, NS, odds from 8 bookmakers; /games?id=23611 resolves Florida State at Louisville, 2026-10-09 23:00, NS, 8 bookmakers. No twins: the laptop holds 104 rows for 104 games in the next seven days and no natural-key cluster. The host's fixtures file of 2026-10-08 16:00Z holds no pairing twice, and its 58 announced kickoffs equal the laptop's."
  - **Cause (verbatim):** "So on #377 it is neither (A) nor (B) as written. The provider's listing no longer carries games that have not started; the games still answer by id (the five of 2026-10-08 did, under the same ids). The laptop had read 91 of Saturday's 95 announced times by 2026-10-06, so the change is later than that. The host's placeholders are games whose time was announced after the host last read them." This settles the cause question above: neither (a) nor (b); the listing reads alone cannot meet the invariant, so the "Limit" bullet's twin case does not arise from these games.
  - **Ruling (verbatim):** "For NCAA, the kickoff, status and score of every stored SCHEDULED game kicking off in the next seven days are refreshed from the provider by the game's own id, at least once a day on the host and in the laptop's morning chain. The listing reads stay: they find games we do not hold. A game the provider does not return by id is never guessed and never deleted: it is counted and listed, and nothing else is done to it."
    - "Amend #378, do not replace it: the ncaa-schedule chain keeps its forward-week listing reads and gains the refresh by id, a command of its own. The timer stays as built."
    - "One GET per game. A rate-limited answer is deferred and retried, never dropped (the sync-odds-football rule)."
    - "The run prints and receipts: asked, unchanged, updated, kickoff moved (each with both times), not found (each listed)."
    - "The test that fails on today's chain: a stored SCHEDULED game in the next seven days that the listing omits and whose answer by id carries another kickoff; after the chain the stored kickoff is the provider's."
    - "The window service is unchanged in this PR."
    - "Addendum 19's invariant stands; this is how it is met. The tag still waits for it."
  - **Built:**
    - New command `refresh-by-id --competition NCAA --days 7` (`cli.py`, logic in `src/ingestion/refresh_by_id.py`). It takes every stored SCHEDULED row of the competition with a kickoff on the UTC dates today .. today+7, the same dates as the chain's listing reads. Each row gets one `GET /games?id=` through the adapter's existing `get_game` (`src/adapters/api_american_football.py`).
    - It applies the kickoff (`utc_date`), the status (the adapter's `_STATUS` map: unknown stays SCHEDULED, law 4) and the score (only when given).
    - The rate-limit rule is sync-odds-football's, on the same constants and seams. Calls are paced at `SP_ODDS_FOOTBALL_RPM` (default 280/min). A `RateLimited` answer (a second 429 inside the adapter) is deferred, then retried after Retry-After (else 60s) for up to `ODDS_RETRY_ROUNDS` = 2 rounds. A game still limited after those rounds is listed and untouched, and the step exits 1.
    - Never guessed: NOT FOUND (an empty answer) is counted, listed and untouched. An answer for different teams is REFUSED and untouched. A lookup error is UNRESOLVED (never read as absent), listed, untouched, and exits 1. A row with no provider id is listed.
    - The receipt is printed (counts line, then each kickoff moved with both times, status and score changes, and each not found / refused / unresolved game). It is also appended to the receipts log (`sp_common.append_receipt`, kind `refresh_by_id`), and the last line is `REFRESH-BY-ID-RECEIPT {counts}`.
    - The `ncaa-schedule` chain is the eight listing reads, then `refresh-by-id --competition NCAA --days 7`. The timer is unchanged.
    - The laptop morning chain (`docs/CLI.md`, "Morning chain (laptop)", Phase 1) runs the same command. That chain is a documented hand-run sequence, not code.
    - The window service, `ncaa-market` and the adapter are unchanged.
  - **Receipts (tests, throwaway DB, fake adapter):**
    - `tests/test_refresh_by_id.py::test_a_scheduled_game_the_listing_omits_gets_the_kickoff_the_provider_answers_by_id` runs the chain's steps as `sp_run.resolve` gives them. On the pre-amendment `ncaa-schedule` it fails with `assert datetime(…, 4, 0) == datetime(…, 23, 30)`: the stored kickoff stays at the 04:00Z placeholder. On the amended chain it passes.
    - Further tests cover a deferred-and-recovered rate limit, a game still rate limited after the rounds (listed, untouched, exit 1), NOT FOUND (listed, untouched), the receipt counts and log line, and the refusal of a non-american-football competition.
    - `tests/test_hosting_pack.py::test_every_day_the_host_refreshes_ncaa_games_by_id` checks that on every weekday some host timer runs `refresh-by-id --competition NCAA --days >= 7`.

**2026-10-09 — RECEIPT BUILT (ARCHITECT, addendum 31 item 2; Issue #354, declared 2026-10-08 addendum 9 item 4): `mlb-actionable-receipt` extended with the declared toss-up splits. Read-only; the operator runs it once after the merge, on the architect's word. No real run exists; nothing has been read. No threshold and no sizing follows from it.**
- **Ruling (verbatim):** "#354: THE DECLARED MLB RECEIPT, BUILT. The acceptance criteria posted on the Issue at 12:55Z today are ACCEPTED as follows. Where the two differ, this decides.
  'The receipt is mlb-actionable-receipt's own, extended, and nothing else in it changes. The parent cohort is the toss-up tier of the regular season, included rows, each word as the receipt already defines it. Two splits of that cohort and no other: by the calendar month of the first pitch's date in America/New_York, and by pick side, HOME or AWAY. A cell prints what a tier row prints today, and its wins. Under each split the cells' games and wins are summed beside the parent row's, and the command exits non-zero if they differ; a row with no first-pitch date is a cell of its own, never dropped. The toss-up rows left out for want of a book close are counted under the same split, by reason. The postseason's toss-up rows get one line of their own, never pooled. The blend split stays as Q3 built it.'
  One test for each split and one for the refusal, on the throwaway DB. The operator runs it once after the merge, on my word, and I read it then. No threshold and no sizing follows from it."
- **Built as ruled.** Parent = the regular table's toss-up / all row (stage regular, tier toss-up, included), the same filter. Month = `Match.utc_date` (naive UTC) converted to America/New_York, `YYYY-MM`; `no first-pitch date` is its own cell, printed even when empty. Pick side = the receipt's top pick (HOME on a tie). Each cell: n, wins, mean model p, mean close fair p, hit rate, hit − close (pp), bootstrap 95% CI (the receipt's B and seed), ROI @ close fair, and the left-out count by reason. Under each split `Σ cells: games, wins · parent: games, wins · reconciled|DIFFERS`; on DIFFERS the command prints, refuses (exit 2) and writes no receipt file. The postseason's toss-up rows: one table line, with its own left-out count. The existing output is unchanged (a byte-identical prefix of the new one on both test fixtures); the blend split is untouched.
- **Readings (where the 12:55Z criteria and the ruling differ, the ruling followed):** (1) the criteria's blend reclassification ("blended only when ... the bookmaker input actually changed the final probability") is not built: the blend split stays as Q3 built it (`market_blend.applied`); (2) no blend cut is crossed with month or side: two splits and no other; (3) "calendar month" is the first pitch's ET date (the criteria named no zone); (4) "reconcile every cell back to the parent" is the ruling's sum of games and wins under each split, exit non-zero on a difference; (5) the criteria's per-cell "missing-close exclusions" are the ruling's left-out rows by reason under the same split. Accepted from the criteria, not differing: each cell carries the denominator, wins, mean model p, win rate, difference from the close fair p and the interval; the new section states the close is a retrospective reference and ROI @ close fair is not an executable return, and that no threshold or sizing follows.
- **Readings (silent in both):** "left out for want of a book close" = every exclusion `grade_row` records for a row with a tier (no close / unpriced; not a book close; no close fair on the pick side); a null-probability row has no tier and is never toss-up. Stage-unknown toss-up rows are neither regular nor postseason: in neither split nor the postseason line (they remain in the existing stage-unknown table). The left-out counts are printed, not reconciled (the ruling's refusal is on games and wins).
- Issue #354: the PR says `Refs #354`; the read closes nothing yet.

**2026-10-09 — FINDING (ARCHITECT addendum 23 item 3 F(3), logged, nothing built; Issue #389; #385): the export shows the latest Kalshi snapshot per leg, not a capture session as books have, so a leg skipped as wide still shows its older quote.** The ruling: "(3) the export shows the latest Kalshi snapshot per leg, not a capture session as books have, so a leg skipped as wide still shows its older quote. (3) is the real fix for A5 and it is an export contract change: gate-class, later."
- Books: the export reads the LAST CAPTURE SESSION (`src/walters/close.py:56` `last_capture`, the close contract: the rows of the last capture session before the start).
- Kalshi: per selection, the latest pre-start snapshot, whatever run captured it: the MLB/soccer predictions export (src/walters/export.py:192-207, `kalshi_by_match[...]` keeps the first row per selection in `captured_at DESC` order), the fixtures export (src/walters/export.py:1122-1128), and NFL (src/walters/nfl_predict.py:276 via `src/walters/venue.py:229` `latest_kalshi_by_selection`). The legs carried into `kalshi_legs` and the K-track quotes can therefore come from different syncs.
- Why a leg goes old: the Kalshi sync skips a leg whose spread is wider than `max_spread` and stores nothing for it (src/ingestion/kalshi_sync.py:440-443, `wide_spread += 1; continue`), so that leg's previous snapshot stays the latest and the export still shows it.
- In #385 (A5) the closing run requires fresh only the legs the Desk read; a stale unread leg is listed in the receipt (`stale_legs_not_read`). The real fix is an export contract change (a Kalshi capture session per game): gate-class, later.

**2026-10-09 — ACCOUNT (ARCHITECT addendum 31 item 4; nothing built): THE HOST AND THE CLOSING RUNS (C7). This entry says what `closing-run` and `closing-watch` would do on the host as they stand on main a63a837, with a file and line for every point. It ends with a proposal for the architect's ruling.**
- **Ruling (verbatim, addendum 31 item 4):** "THE HOST AND THE CLOSING RUNS (C7): AN ACCOUNT FROM THE CODE, NOTHING BUILT. One ledger entry, a file and line for every point, and a proposal at the end. I rule from it. C7 stands: the cutover ruling decides when anything runs on the host. Say what closing-run and closing-watch would do on the host exactly as they stand today: - The mirror push. push_mirror names the role laptop. What does the host's push need, and from which setting? - The backup. backup_folder and todays_backup (sports_<date>*.db in SP_BACKUP_DIR or ~/backups) against where and under what names sp_backup.py writes on the host. Would a closing run find the host's backup of the day, or take its own every day? - The page: the screen notification off macOS, and the phone page through the host's card topic. - The lock: a closing run against the hourly window service and the timed chains. How long do those hold it, and what does a wait until T-5 mean there? - MLB. SP_SKIP_FAMILIES on the host names MLB: what the watch does with every MLB first pitch as built, and what closing-watch --family NFL --family SOCCER does instead. - The receipts and their release field, and the settings the host would need in host.env, by name only. - What a timer unit beside the existing ones would be, and what install.sh would have to enable. - What the laptop's watch must stop covering on the day the host starts, so that no game is paged twice."
- **Before the bullets, two facts.**
  - **The host cannot run closing-run today.** Production is the tag (CLAUDE.md, release model), and the newest tag, v1.3.0, does not hold `deploy/hosting/closing.py` (`git cat-file -e v1.3.0:deploy/hosting/closing.py`: "exists on disk, but not in 'v1.3.0'"). Everything below describes main a63a837 as it would run once a tag carries it.
  - **No host unit exists for it.** chains.py:345-346: "The host runs NFL and SOCCER with the same command under a timer from the cutover ruling on, not before." No timer ships. scripts/setup_closing_watch.sh:6 says the same, and that script is launchd only (`~/Library/LaunchAgents`, `launchctl`, `osascript`: :33-35, :104-135, :141).
- **1. The mirror push.**
  - As built, `push_mirror` runs `exports_mirror.py push --role laptop --label <label>` with the role hard-coded (deploy/hosting/closing.py:412-416). It runs after every successful page (closing.py:1521-1523) and once at install (`install-push`, closing.py:1829-1831).
  - An explicit `--role` overrides the script's default role, which is read from `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE` (deploy/hosting/exports_mirror.py:273). So the host's `host.env` setting `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE=host` (docs/specs/exports-mirror.md:52-55) is never consulted.
  - **What a host push as built would do:**
    - It copies the host's exports/ into `laptop/<date>/` and `laptop/latest/` of the mirror (exports_mirror.py:191-199).
    - It deletes every `laptop/latest/*` file whose kind the host does not hold (:200-203).
    - It prunes `laptop/` dated folders (:204-206).
    - The compare Action then reads host files under the laptop's name (exports-mirror.md:30-32).
  - **What the host's push needs:** `--role host`, from `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE`. That is the setting the chains' hook already reads: `mirror_after_step` passes `--role c.setting("SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE") or "host"` (deploy/hosting/sp_run.py:291-293).
  - Push and remote are gated by `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_REMOTE`. When it is unset the run is refused before any step (M1, closing.py:1136-1141, :1171).
  - The deploy key is `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_KEY`, else `/etc/sports-predictor/exports_deploy_key`, else `~sp/.ssh/sp_exports_deploy_key` (exports_mirror.py:62-70). An SSH remote with no key file is refused (:91-102, :287-290).
  - The working clone is `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_DIR`, default `logs/exports-mirror` (:291). That is the same clone the chains' hook uses.
  - The code cannot say whether the host's `host.env` holds the remote today. Only the host's `kind: mirror` receipts would show it (sp_run.py:294-303).
- **2. The backup.**
  - **The closing run's side:**
    - `backup_folder()` is `SP_BACKUP_DIR`, else `~/backups` (closing.py:457-460). It is read through `sp_common.setting`: the environment, then `host.env`, then the checkout's `.env` (deploy/hosting/sp_common.py:66-75).
    - `todays_backup()` takes the first non-empty `sports_<day>*.db` in that folder (closing.py:463-470), where `<day>` is the run's **America/New_York** date at the moment it holds the lock (closing.py:1382-1383, ny_date :145-147).
  - **The host's side:**
    - `host.env` sets `SP_BACKUP_DIR=/var/backups/sports-predictor` (deploy/hosting/etc/host.env.example:7). install.sh creates that folder as sp:sp 0700 (deploy/hosting/install.sh:9).
    - The two defaults differ, but neither is reached on the host: sp_backup's own default is `~/backups/sports-predictor` (deploy/hosting/sp_backup.py:27-28), closing's is `~/backups`.
    - sp_backup writes `sports_<UTC date>.db` (sp_backup.py:31-35, :43-44). A second backup that day becomes `sports_<date>_<HHMMSS>.db` (:45-46). Event backups are `sports_<date>_prerefresh_<HHMM>.db` / `_precleanup_` (:33-34). Each has a `.sha256` sidecar (:67).
  - **When the host's daily exists:**
    - The first one of a UTC day is taken by the first `backup: daily` chain: intl-daily at 07:20 UTC (deploy/hosting/systemd/sp-intl-daily.timer:7; chains.py:170-171; sp_run.py:449-452), or weekly-fullseason at Sun 06:00 UTC (sp-weekly-fullseason.timer:7; chains.py:219-220).
    - sp-backup.service then takes one at 09:30 UTC regardless (sp-backup.timer:7; sp_backup.py:97-102). Because the file exists, that one is named `_HHMMSS`.
  - **Answer: a closing run finds the host's backup, with one exception.**
    - Same folder (both read `SP_BACKUP_DIR` from `host.env`), and the glob matches sp_backup's names.
    - After 00:00 UTC the New York date is still the previous day, whose UTC-dated file exists (taken at 07:20 UTC that day). So an evening run finds it.
    - **The exception:** a run that holds the lock between New York midnight (04:00 UTC under EDT, 05:00 UTC under EST) and the first daily at 07:20 UTC (06:00 on Sundays). Unless an event backup of that date already exists (a `sports_<NY date>_prerefresh_*.db` or `_precleanup_*.db` from a soccer-refresh or cleanup run after New York midnight, which `todays_backup`'s glob accepts, closing.py:463-470 and (a) below), that run finds no `sports_<NY date>*.db` and takes its own `sports_<date>.db` (closing.py:488-531).
    - sp_run's `todays_daily()` would then accept that file as the day's daily, because the sidecar format matches (closing.py:524; sp_backup.py:84-94). sp-backup.service still writes its own `_HHMMSS` copy.
    - Whether any NFL or PL start time puts a lock in that window is a fact of the fixture list. The code does not decide it.
  - **Three differences as built:**
    - (a) `todays_backup` counts a `_prerefresh_`/`_precleanup_` event backup as the day's backup and does not check the sidecar. sp_backup's `todays_daily` excludes `_pre` and checks the sha (sp_backup.py:89-93).
    - (b) A closing backup that finds the plain name taken is `sports_<date>_closing_<HHMMSS>.db` (closing.py:494-496). sp_prune counts it as a daily toward the 14 kept (deploy/hosting/sp_prune.py:25, :30-36). pull_backup never pulls it (deploy/hosting/pull_backup.py:33).
    - (c) The folder is sp-only (install.sh:9). A closing run started by hand as another user fails as `backup` whenever it must take one.
- **3. The page.**
  - **The screen:**
    - `notify()` posts only on macOS. Elsewhere it prints `· notification (not macOS, not posted)` and returns `{"posted": False, "skipped": "not macOS"}` (closing.py:373-377).
    - The receipt records it under `page.screen` (closing.py:1514-1520). B2 says it "is recorded and changes nothing" (closing.py:115-116). `exit` is set to 0 because the phone page went out (closing.py:1510-1513, :1521).
    - The same applies to the failure and miss notices: their screen half is skipped and their phone half still goes (closing.py:1263-1277, :1318-1330).
  - **The phone:**
    - `page_phone()` POSTs to `sp_notify.ntfy_url("NTFY_CARD_TOPIC")` (closing.py:387-404). That URL is `NTFY_SERVER` (default https://ntfy.sh) plus the topic (deploy/hosting/sp_notify.py:62-73), read through `setting` and then the checkout's `.env` (sp_notify.py:44-45).
    - It tries three times, ten seconds apart (closing.py:1497-1507). If ntfy never accepts, the run fails as `page` and nothing is pushed (closing.py:1510-1513).
    - On the host the card topic lives in the checkout's `.env` (docs/specs/hosting-h1.md:509). The window service's delta pages already use that topic (deploy/hosting/sp_window_page.py:312-320).
    - So host closing pages would arrive in the same ntfy topic as the hourly card deltas, and the laptop's closing pages use that same topic too.
    - Closing pages have no quiet hours (the window pager's 00:00-07:00 ET rule, hosting-h1.md:496-499, is not in closing.py).
    - A page does not say which machine sent it: `page_text` is built from the family, the start time and the games (closing.py:931). The receipt carries `host` (sp_common.py:199).
  - When the topic is unset or holds whitespace, the run is refused before any step (C6, closing.py:1144-1155).
- **4. The lock.**
  - **The lock file:** closing takes `c.db_lock()` (closing.py:432-435), which is the same flock as every chain and sp_backup: `SP_LOCK=/var/lib/sports-predictor/db.lock` (host.env.example:6; sp_common.py:82-83, :211-229). The lock is polled every 5 s (sp_common.py:225).
  - **How long the window service holds it:**
    - It fires hourly at :05, except 04 and 05 UTC (deploy/hosting/systemd/sp-window.timer:10).
    - It holds the lock for the backup check plus every planned step (sp_run.py:449-460).
    - Inside that hold, each step can add a mirror push of up to 90 s (sp_run.py:219, :277, :284-305) and transient retries of 15 s + 45 s (sp_run.py:218, :256-268).
    - It then takes the lock again for each `freshen:<family>` it triggers (sp_run.py:348-349) and for the re-card (sp_run.py:473-475).
  - **How long the timed chains hold it:** the same way, under `sp-chain@.service`.
  - **The bound:** no step has a timeout (sp_run.py:186-201). The only bound on a hold is the unit's `TimeoutStartSec=3h` (deploy/hosting/systemd/sp-chain@.service:23). How long a run actually takes is not in the code. The host's `kind: chain` receipts carry `duration_s` (sp_run.py:476-479).
  - **Timed chains near the closing windows** (systemd units, UTC unless named):
    - soccer-prematch at Sat 10:30 Europe/London (sp-soccer-saturday.timer:7), 85 minutes before a 12:30 UK kickoff's T-35 at 11:55.
    - nhl-daily at 16:00 (sp-nhl-daily.timer:7), 25 minutes before a Sunday 13:00 ET kickoff's T-35 at 16:25.
    - nfl-lines at 15:00 (sp-nfl-lines.timer:7) and nfl-predict at Sun 14:00 (sp-nfl-predict.timer:8).
    - ncaa-market at Sat 13:00 (sp-ncaa-market.timer:15); ncaa-schedule at 10:35/22:35 (sp-ncaa-schedule.timer:10).
    - backup at 09:30 (sp-backup.timer:7; it takes the lock, sp_backup.py:51).
  - **What a wait until T-5 means:**
    - A watch-started run waits at most `start − 5 min − now` (closing.py:1658-1660). That is at most 30 minutes from T-35.
    - If it gets the lock in time, it runs then. Its page goes out after T-30, and its price check uses the moment it holds the lock (closing.py:1544-1550, :1459).
    - If not, it records a `closing_miss` "the lock was held until inside T-5", notified once (closing.py:1667-1672). If it gets the lock inside T-5, the miss reads "the lock came inside T-5" (closing.py:1561-1564).
    - A miss is not an attempt (closing.py:240-243). So the next tick finds the same start time inside T-5 and records a second miss, "inside T-5 when the watch saw it" (closing.py:1750-1756). These are two notices for one start time, which B6's once-per-reason rule allows (closing.py:1318-1326).
    - The watch runs its due start times one after another inside one tick (closing.py:1757-1768). A run waiting for the lock delays the other family's due start time in the same tick. With systemd, a oneshot that is still running is not started again by its timer. On the laptop, launchd likewise does not start a second instance of a running job.
  - A manual `closing-run` waits up to db_lock's default of 3 h (closing.py:1658; sp_common.py:212).
- **5. MLB.**
  - **What the host's data holds:** the host stores MLB games through mlb-history (chains.py:64-76; sp-mlb-history.timer on T11, hosting-h1.md:711). `host.env` names MLB in `SP_SKIP_FAMILIES` (host.env.example:23).
  - **Bare `closing-watch`, as built:**
    - It plans all three families (closing.py:1713), and it plans MLB anyway (closing.py:1715-1721).
    - It records no inside-T-5 miss for MLB (:1752-1753) and skips the feed check (:1760).
    - For each MLB start time (a group of first pitches within 10 minutes, closing.py:204-218) that enters T-35..T-5, it calls `run()` (:1767).
    - `run()` refuses at the second check (closing.py:1169-1172, :1117-1123): "laptop only: SP_SKIP_FAMILIES names MLB here (the host cannot reach the MLB feed)". That refusal is receipted (exit 2) and notified with high priority through the card topic (closing.py:1280-1295, :1263-1277). This happens once per MLB start time per day.
    - Later ticks for the same start time refuse silently (closing.py:1287-1289). But they still return 2 (closing.py:1768), so the tick exits 2 on every minute of each MLB start time's 30-minute window.
    - A unit carrying `OnFailure=sp-notify@…` like every sp unit would page `NTFY_TOPIC` on each of those ticks. That is about 30 pages per start time.
  - **`closing-watch --family NFL --family SOCCER` instead:** MLB is never planned (closing.py:1713-1715; cli.py:8640-8653). There is no read of MLB, no MLB receipt and no MLB page.
  - **`preflight`, as built:**
    - It always checks all three families (closing.py:1787-1792), and `main` passes it no families (closing.py:1822-1823).
    - On the host it therefore refuses because of MLB, whatever the unit runs.
- **6. The receipts, the release field and the settings.**
  - **Receipt kinds:** a `closing` receipt for every success, failure, refusal and superseded run, and a `closing_miss` receipt (closing.py:46-47).
  - **The fields every receipt gets** through `append_receipt` (sp_common.py:195-208):
    - `ts`.
    - `host`: `SP_HOST_NAME`, i.e. sp-vps-1 (host.env.example:4).
    - `release` (`running_release`, sp_common.py:143-161):
      - the tag (e.g. `v1.4.0`) when the host's HEAD sits on it, as the host deploys tags;
      - `BETA <branch>@<sha>` on a branch, `UNTAGGED@<sha>` when detached;
      - null with `release_error` when git is unreadable (sp_common.py:201-203; safe.directory for the root-owned checkout, :125-140).
    - `writer_of_record`: `laptop` on the host until the cutover flip (host.env.example:19; sp_common.py:171-174).
  - **Where they go:** on the host, `SP_RECEIPTS=/var/log/sports-predictor/receipts.jsonl` (host.env.example:5; sp_common.py:78-79).
  - **What reads them:** the closing state reads that same file and only that file: attempts, `covered_ids`, refusal and miss de-duplication, and the last calls (closing.py:223-250, :274-310, :1287, :1324, :1075). Nothing filters by `host` or `release`.
  - **In sp_receipts' pasted table:** a closing line shows as `closing` with an empty key line and an empty duration, because closing writes `seconds`, not `duration_s` (deploy/hosting/sp_receipts.py:32-56, :96-104; closing.py:1540).
  - **Settings the host would need, by name.**
    - Already in host.env.example: `SP_BACKUP_DIR`, `SP_LOCK`, `SP_RECEIPTS`, `SP_HOST_NAME`, `SP_WRITER_OF_RECORD`, `SP_SKIP_FAMILIES` (host.env.example:4-7, :19, :23).
    - In host.env by the mirror spec, but not in host.env.example: `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_REMOTE` (required, M1) and `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE` (exports-mirror.md:52-55). `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_KEY` is needed only for a non-default key path. `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_DIR` is optional.
    - In the checkout's `.env`: `NTFY_CARD_TOPIC` (required, C6; hosting-h1.md:509), optionally `NTFY_SERVER`, and `DATABASE_URL`. `db_path` reads `DATABASE_URL` from the environment or `.env` only, never `host.env` (sp_common.py:232-241).
  - **Settings that do not apply:** `SP_PARALLEL_MODE`/`SP_DESIGNATED_DAYS` do not reach closing steps. Closing calls `sp_run.run_step` directly (closing.py:427-429), not `run_steps`, which is where the metered skip, the transient retries and the per-step mirror hook live (sp_run.py:242-281).
- **7. A timer unit, and install.sh.**
  - **What the code fixes about such a unit:**
    - It cannot be `sp-chain@<chain>`: sp_run refuses the closing chains ("closing_only", sp_run.py:403-418).
    - It would be its own `sp-closing-watch.service` plus `sp-closing-watch.timer`, on the pattern of sp-backup.service (User/Group sp, WorkingDirectory /opt/sports-predictor, `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/sports-predictor/host.env`, Type=oneshot; sp-backup.service:6-17).
    - Its ExecStart would be `venv/bin/python cli.py closing-watch` with the families.
    - TimeoutStartSec must cover one tick that waits up to 30 minutes and then runs a chain that has no step timeout.
  - **What CI fixes:**
    - Every timer must carry `OnCalendar=` lines of the form `[days ]*-*-* H:MM:00 TZ` with a literal two-digit minute, outside 04:15-05:15 UTC (tests/test_hosting_pack.py:107-131). A per-minute `*:*` calendar or an `OnUnitActiveSec=` timer fails that test as written.
    - Every shipped `*.timer` must be named in the T11 list, `TIMERS` or `MLB_LAPTOP_ONLY` (tests/test_hosting_pack.py:388-396; hosting-h1.md:708-718). There is no "shipped, not enabled until a ruling" list for a closing timer to join.
    - `sp_notify.unit_for` maps an unknown instance to `sp-chain@<instance>.service` (sp_notify.py:26-29). An `OnFailure=sp-notify@closing-watch` would therefore read the wrong unit's journal unless that mapping is added.
  - **install.sh:**
    - It copies every `systemd/*.service` and `*.timer` (install.sh:14), so a new unit is installed with no change. It enables nothing by design (install.sh:2-4, :16).
    - Enabling happens in the runbook: `systemctl enable --now` plus an append to `/etc/sports-predictor/timers.enabled` (hosting-h1.md:713-715, :740-747).
    - `sp_deploy.py` does not install unit files (hosting-h1.md:749-751).
    - `timers.enabled` is the list sp_cutover's pause and resume stop and start (deploy/hosting/sp_cutover.py:16, :21, :69).
    - So install.sh has nothing to enable. The enable is a runbook step under the cutover ruling.
- **8. The laptop's watch on the day the host starts.**
  - **What the laptop runs now:** the laptop's job runs `closing-watch` with no `--family` (scripts/setup_closing_watch.sh:111-116), so it covers MLB, NFL and SOCCER.
  - **Why both machines would page:** each machine decides from its own receipts file (sp_common.py:78-79; closing.py:223-250). Neither sees the other's success. Every NFL kickoff and every PL kickoff covered by both watches would be closed and paged twice, on the same card topic (section 3), and pushed twice.
  - **What the laptop must stop covering:** every NFL and every SOCCER (PL) start time, from the moment the host's timer is enabled. The laptop keeps MLB, which is laptop only (closing.py:1120-1121).
  - **The setup script cannot express that today:**
    - It writes no `--family` into the plist and takes none (setup_closing_watch.sh:20-21, :111-116).
    - Its preflight checks all three families (closing.py:1787-1792, :1823).
  - **What the code does not guard:**
    - Nothing in the code stops a hand-run `closing-run --family NFL` on the laptop after the switch.
    - Nothing in the code chooses the switch moment. The code has no cross-machine check, so the moment must not fall inside any NFL or PL start time's T-35..T-0.
  - **"was" restarts on the host.** The host's first page computes it from the host's receipts and the host's exports/ only (closing.py:1059-1112). It does not use what the laptop last paged.
- **Proposal (for the architect's ruling; C7 stands: the cutover ruling decides when anything runs on the host, and nothing below is enabled before it).**
  - P1, the role:
    - `push_mirror` and `install-push` take `--role` from `SP_EXPORTS_MIRROR_ROLE`, as `mirror_after_step` does.
    - It is unset or not host|laptop: the run is refused before any step, like M1, and preflight says so. There is no default and no guess (law 4).
    - One test: on the host settings, the push argv names host.
  - P2, the watch command: the host's unit runs `closing-watch --family NFL --family SOCCER`, never bare (section 5). preflight takes the same `--family` list.
  - P3, the units:
    - Ship `sp-closing-watch.service` and `sp-closing-watch.timer` disabled. The timer has one `OnCalendar` per minute over hours 00..03,06..23 UTC (the window timer's hours), `Persistent=false` and `AccuracySec=1s`.
    - The watch notifies its own refusals, misses and run failures, but only once its Python process is running: an import or startup failure, an unhandled exception and a `TimeoutStartSec` kill never reach that code. So the service keeps an external failure path: `OnFailure=sp-notify@closing-watch.service` (the house pattern, sp-chain@.service:7), with `SuccessExitStatus=2` so that a refusal the watch has already receipted and notified (exit 2, closing.py:1281-1290) does not page again every minute (section 5). `sp_notify.unit_for` maps an unknown instance to `sp-chain@<instance>.service` (sp_notify.py:26-29), so `closing-watch` needs its own entry there, mapping it to `sp-closing-watch.service`: one line and one test. A bound such as `TimeoutStartSec=2h` is for the architect to set.
    - Amend the T11 test with a third list, held until the cutover ruling. That is a test change, and it is named here so it is ruled, not slipped in.
  - P4, the runbook: a host step written now and run on the cutover ruling's word:
    - first, before anything is enabled: the family-scoped preflight (`--family NFL --family SOCCER`, P2), which runs the mirror, backup-folder and card-topic refusal checks that `closing-watch --dry-run` does not; one `closing.py test-page` as sp; and `closing-watch --family NFL --family SOCCER --dry-run`;
    - only when all three pass: `install`, `daemon-reload`, `enable --now sp-closing-watch.timer`, and the append to `timers.enabled`;
    - The receipts: the preflight, the test page accepted, the dry run, then the timer's next elapse.
  - P5, the laptop:
    - `setup_closing_watch.sh --family MLB` writes the families into the plist and its preflight.
    - On the cutover day the operator reinstalls it with `--family MLB` **before** the host timer is enabled, at a moment when no NFL or PL start time is within 35 minutes. Receipts: the laptop's `closing-watch --dry-run` lists MLB only, then the host's lists NFL and SOCCER.
  - P6, read before ruling (read-only, no build): the host's `kind: chain` `duration_s` for window, soccer-prematch, nhl-daily, nfl-lines and nfl-predict over the parallel weeks. It is an upper bound, not a lock-hold time: the clock starts before `db_lock()` is taken, so it includes any wait for another holder, and it runs on through the window page and the freshens outside the first hold (sp_run.py:443-478). It can show that a chain never holds the lock long enough to matter. It cannot show how often a closing would wait. If it does not settle the question, measuring that needs the lock's own acquire and release times in the receipt: a build, for a ruling. P3's timeout follows from whichever the architect accepts.
  - P7, for a ruling, no build proposed: whether a closing run's own backup should exclude `_pre` event backups and check the sidecar, as sp_backup's `todays_daily` does (section 2(a)).
  - Left as built: the screen half off macOS (recorded as skipped) and the backup folder and date rule (section 2).

**2026-10-09 — SWEEP (ARCHITECT sweep rule 2026-10-05): four unanswered Codex threads on merged #340 and #310, verified on main 081d9fa; two fixed, two already settled.**
- #310 P1 4200879012 (deploy/hosting/sp_deploy.py checkout): REAL. A post-checkout hook runs after git has moved HEAD and the worktree and only changes the exit status (githooks(5)). The handler receipted "checkout failed — the code stays at <before>" while the target was live, and a retry saw an empty range, so new migrations were never printed. Fix: after a failing checkout, HEAD decides where the code is. With HEAD at the target, the receipt records the move (`to_sha`/`to_release`, `checkout_warning`) and prints the new migrations, but the receipt and the exit stay nonzero (`exit 1`): the hook may not have finished its own work, so a failed hook is never reported as success (Codex P2 4235404516 on #409). Pin: tests/test_codex_sweep_340_310.py::test_failing_post_checkout_hook_after_head_moved_is_receipted_at_the_target_and_fails (on 081d9fa: no migrations recorded, receipt `from_sha` only).
- #310 P2 4200879018 (sp_deploy._classify): REAL. pip's break_args_options splits options at the first "-"-prefixed word, past the `;`, so `pkg>=1; python_version >= "3.0" --config-settings=key=value` carries the option; the classifier scanned only the text before the marker and called it a plain specifier. Fix: options are read across the whole line. Pin: tests/test_codex_sweep_340_310.py::test_per_requirement_option_after_a_marker_is_refused (fails on 081d9fa).
- #340 P2 4211712341 (scripts/odds_payload_probe.py, `values: [null]` / `["bad"]` / `[{}]`): already fixed on main. `usable_quotes` (9324e3c) counts only quotes the adapter would turn into odds rows, and f53b611 makes the verdict use it; all three payloads read INCONCLUSIVE on 081d9fa.
- #340 P2 4211712334 (src/walters/venue_quote_age.py, `mode=ro` WAL sidecars): reproduced (SQLite 3.45.1 creates `-wal` / `-shm` for a `mode=ro` reader of a checkpointed WAL DB) but settled by design in 0c87fe1. That commit replaced an `immutable=1` open with `mode=ro` because immutable skips change detection (a torn read during an app write or checkpoint, from an earlier Codex finding on the same PR). The READ-ONLY guarantee there is about the DB content. Nothing changed. If a zero-sidecar guarantee is wanted, that is an architect call, since it would undo 0c87fe1's trade-off.
- No gate, threshold, verdict or prediction output moves.

- **Codex round 1 on #385 (four findings, all verified real, fixed with fail-before tests):**
  - P1 `target moved` (SUPERSEDED by addendum 23 C, below: a moved game now leaves the run): a schedule read that moves a covered game off its start (still SCHEDULED) failed nothing, and the run could page it under the old start or succeed with zero rows. Now an own-check failure `target moved`, receipted with each game's target, covered start and stored start; export moved out, no push, no call page. Reading (conservative): a partial move fails the run too, naming only the moved games. Watch behaviour, read from the code: receipts are keyed by start time, so the new start is a separate key with zero attempts. After a full move the old start forms no group and is not retried; after a partial move the old start is retried (up to three attempts) with only the games still there, and that retry is not pointless. `covered_ids` no longer counts a game an attempt found moved, so the old start's later success or third attempt does not mark it closed.
  - P1 `watch`: `now` was reassigned at the top of `watch`, so every queued run in a tick got the tick's time. Each run now reads `clock()` when it starts; a test-supplied `now` still fixes it.
  - P2 `sync-injuries --strict`: a missing competition under `--kickoff-within-hours` returned exit 0 at the empty-window branch; it now fails as a strict read. Note: `sync-matches` on a competition not in the DB does exit 0 (`service.sync_matches` returns `skipped = len(matches)` after the provider call); left unchanged.
  - P2 `parse_utc`: a `-hh:mm` offset was truncated and the local time read as UTC; any explicit offset now converts to UTC.
